title: 《壁画迷境》开发商访谈：离开迪士尼，Dlala 第一次讲自己的童话
text:
重构童话
8 月 25 日，gamescom 开幕夜直播的舞台上，Dlala Studios 放出了新作《壁画迷境（Murals）》的首支预告。
对这家来自英国埃塞克斯、成立 14 年的独立工作室来说，这次亮相是一个全新的开始：《壁画迷境》是他们十多年来第一个完全原创的 IP，也是第一次由自己来发行一款游戏。从 2020 年给 Xbox 做《忍者蛙（Battletoads）》，到 2023 年给迪士尼做的《迪士尼幻梦岛（Disney Illusion Island）》，Dlala 的手艺里始终带着别人的 IP。
而这一次，他们把大家熟悉的童话“彻底搞坏”—— 睡美人已经好几个星期没被允许睡觉，长发公主的头发变成了要她命的东西，汉塞尔与格蕾特走进那座糖果屋之后，故事开始朝完全失控的方向跑。
在 gamescom 开幕前，Dlala 办了一场线上媒体交流会，CEO、游戏总监兼联合编剧 Aj Grand-Scrutton 亲自演示并回答提问；随后我们又通过邮件问答形式，围绕诡饰系统、战斗平衡与首次自主发行等话题做了追问。以下为访谈内容整理。
Dlala 主创团队，分别为 Aj Grand-Scrutton、Ben Waring、Loukia Kyriakidou、Grant Allen、Marcus Purvis 记者：先从一个最基础的问题开始。《壁画迷境》到底是一款怎样的游戏？它和你们前两部作品相比，变化在哪里？
Aj： 简单说，这是一款等距视角的动作冒险游戏，你在一个个“彻底出了错”的童话世界里砍杀、战斗。我们喜欢说它是“fairy tales gone spectacularly wrong”—— 童话彻底出了大错。
对我们来说，这一步其实是顺其自然。做《忍者蛙》的时候，我们做的是横版格斗，战斗占了很大比重；到了《迪士尼幻梦岛》，我们想试试完全不同的东西，于是做了一款没有任何战斗的类银河城。等到要规划下一款游戏时，我们觉得是时候回到战斗了 —— 但这次想做一款更偏武器、更容易上手、拿起就玩的等距视角冒险。
记者：玩家在游戏里的身份是什么？这次的主角设定似乎和以往不太一样。
Aj： 你扮演的是一位失忆的英雄。游戏一开场，你醒过来，发现自己被困在《睡美人》的城堡里，不记得自己是谁，也不知道怎么出去。你唯一的同伴是乐福（Loaf），一个从画里活过来的家伙。
这个主角我们叫他“近乎沉默的主角”。他很少说话，每次开口，都是通过对话选项交给玩家来决定。你可以做个正直到有点老好人的英雄，也可以保持中立，甚至整局游戏里一有机会就做个彻头彻尾的混蛋。你想成为什么样的英雄，完全由你决定。
乐福就不一样了，他话多得要命。它打架不行，但在沟通上简直是弥补了所有短板，游戏里大部分剧情都是通过它和其他角色的对话展开的。玩过我们前作的人应该知道，我们从来不忌讳让角色打破第四面墙 —— 乐福尤其如此。
记者：把童话“改坏”这件事，你们具体是怎么做的？怎么避免变成那种“为了反转而反转“？
Aj： 是个好问题。我甚至可以说得更直白一点：很多作品里的反转本身就挺廉价的，游戏里尤其多。有一种手法我特别讨厌 —— 先明明白白告诉你某个人是好人，然后突然来个反转，说他其实是坏人。我们绝对不能这么干。
首席编剧 Kelsy Abbott 在这点上盯我盯得很紧。游戏里的角色可以根据自己掌握的信息形成判断，比如乐福可以觉得“这人应该是好人”，但作为游戏本身，我们不会先告诉玩家“这个角色就是好人”，过一会儿再翻脸说“其实不是”。
具体到每个故事，我们的处理方式都不一样。有些故事我们喜欢几乎整个原作，《睡美人》就是这样 —— 我们对它的颠覆，是从“她已经好几个星期没被允许睡觉”这个设定开始的，但整个世界和背景还是相当忠于原作。而《糖果屋》就完全不一样了，我们保留了最开始那个出发点 —— 两个孩子发现一座糖果做的房子，但从那之后，事情就开始彻底变得古怪，场景、角色、故事全都往另一个方向跑了。
记者：那在这么多童话里，团队是怎么挑出要改编哪些的？是看个人喜好，还是看改编空间？
Aj： 两边都有。我们最开始是让团队所有人一起回想，自己小时候真正喜欢过哪些故事——既包括原始童话文本，也包括后来各种改编版本。然后我们再想：哪些故事是我们有信心做好，而且能做出属于 Dlala 自己的版本的？
我们不想只是因为某个故事本身很酷，就拿过来简单用一下。我们希望玩家能明显感觉到：这是 Dlala 对这个故事的理解。有些故事我们拿原作当起点，逐渐走向自己的版本；有些则从一开始就往完全不同的方向写。还有些故事，我们喜欢它们世界观的深度，但觉得角色不太适合放进一款 Dlala 的游戏里；反过来，也有些故事真正吸引我们的其实就是角色。
记者：说说战斗吧。你们把战斗定位成这款游戏的核心支柱，这个系统是怎么搭起来的？
Aj： 对，战斗始终是核心（Combat At Its Core），这是我们开发过程中一直贴在墙上的原则之一。我们做的每一件事，都得先过一遍这个判断：它到底有没有在服务战斗体验？
武器方面，我们没有走那种“一大堆武器、越拿越强”的路线，而是做了一小批更聚焦的武器。它们更像是风格选择，而不是数值升级。比如速度和力量都很均衡的单手剑，属于全能型；如果你想要更慢、更重、砸起来更爽的，那就选战锤。玩家选武器，想的是“哪个更像我喜欢打战斗游戏的方式”，而不是“哪个更强”。
我们参考了不少东西。喜欢《暗黑破坏神》《流放之路》这类大型动作 RPG 的玩家会找到熟悉的东西，喜欢《堡垒》这类独立动作游戏的玩家也会。战斗打起来挺狂热、挺混乱，但你始终能感觉到自己掌控着局面。特别要说的是，我们不是 Roguelike —— 这是一款线性的冒险游戏，这一点我们想从一开始就说清楚。
记者：诡饰（Eeries）是这套战斗系统里最让人好奇的部分。能具体讲讲它是什么吗？
Aj： 很高兴能聊到这个机制，不过有些内容我还是想留到后面的宣传节点再展开。现在能说的是，诡饰是一种会明显改变你战斗方式的道具，分成两类：武器诡饰直接作用于你的近战或远程武器，改变攻击效果；英雄诡饰则作用于角色本身。比如有的可以把一次攻击的伤害平均分给当前区域里的所有敌人，另一些则让你在敌人受伤时回血，哪怕伤害不是你亲手打的。
诡饰由一位叫“魔法戴夫（Magic Dave）”的角色提供。你在关卡里遇到他的时候，他会从一个随机池里抽出三件诡饰，让你选一件。大多数诡饰都是这样随机获得的。
记者：诡饰是随机的，玩家会不会因此拿到一堆不想要的东西？构筑空间有多大？
Aj： 我一直相信一句话：限制本身反而能激发创造力。正因为槽位有限，而游戏又会提供大量不同的诡饰，玩家反而更容易冒出“要不我换掉这个，试试另外几个放一块会怎么样”的念头。诡饰的效果往往非常明显、很有反馈感，所以这种“换一个试试”的冲动会自然地鼓励玩家去尝试不同的组合。
当然，有些玩家根本不想这么玩，我们也不希望游戏因此惩罚他。诡饰会奖励那些喜欢研究、喜欢构筑的玩家，但不会强迫所有人都必须用这种方式去享受游戏。
记者：既然诡饰有很强的组合空间，你们怎么在“给玩家自由实验”和“保证战斗可控”之间拿捏平衡？
Aj： 可控性主要来自武器。每种武器只提供数量不多、但足够有效的一组攻击，我们不给玩家一长串复杂连招。玩家最核心的那套操作是强力、稳定、好理解的。而真正的实验和定制空间，我们把它留给了诡饰。
这样设计有个很有意思的地方：玩家在整个游戏里用的战斗输入其实是一致的，但这些输入最后产生什么结果，会因为装备的诡饰不同而完全不同。你进入战斗前先决定选什么武器、搭什么诡饰，进入战斗后用的还是那些你最熟悉的操作，但同样一个操作，换个组合可能就是完全不同的效果。这一点到现在都让我们很兴奋。
记者：那平衡性呢？玩家后期会不会凑出过于强大的诡饰组合，导致后期难度反而下降？
Aj： 这个风险百分之百存在。事实上，我们不仅意识到了，某种程度上甚至是主动接受了它。我给团队定的规则很简单，就一句：“这样还好玩吗？”
如果玩家因为某套组合变得特别强，甚至强到有点打破平衡，但这种状态让玩家觉得自己特别厉害，而且游戏并没有因此变无聊，那我完全接受游戏里存在这样的组合。我当然不希望每一套都能把平衡打穿。但如果你正好发现了特别厉害的搭配，又刚好运气好随机到了需要的诡饰 —— 只要你玩得开心，这就没问题。
另外，游戏里诡饰数量相当多。如果你只是从头到尾通关一次，大概只会见到、拿到全部诡饰的一半左右。加上随机分配，玩家并不能保证一定凑出那些最强组合——但这种可能性确实存在，我们觉得这反而是乐趣的一部分。
记者：我注意到游戏的常规战斗里似乎没有掉落回血道具。这是刻意为之吗？是否有其他替代方式，比如通过特定诡饰来实现回血？
Aj： 观察得很细，你的判断是对的。常规战斗里我们不会让敌人掉落回血道具，这是试过几种方案之后有意识做的决定。开发中我们试过让敌人掉血包、在战斗区域放可破坏的回血物件、甚至给玩家一个可充能的治疗药水。
但打磨下来我们发现，《壁画迷境》的重点越来越不是“我得想办法撑过这一整关”，而是“我得解决眼前这一场战斗”。所以我们希望每场战斗遭遇本身就是一个完整的挑战，玩家也知道，打完这场、继续往前走之后，通常还有机会恢复更多生命值。当然，也确实有一些诡饰和组合，能让你在战斗中回血。
记者：这是 Dlala 第一款原创 IP，也是第一次自主发行。相比过去以联合开发或外部合作方的身份做项目，这次最大的挑战是什么？
Aj： 简单来说，挑战有很多。（笑）
大家常有一种印象，觉得没有发行商在旁边把控，开发团队很容易把项目越做越大、范围失控、预算超支。但我们实际情况正好相反。我们对自己非常严格，一直在确保《壁画迷境》是一款非常清楚自己要做什么的游戏。我们不想因为有了更多自主权，就把它不断做大，最后变成一个什么都想塞进去的项目。这种"知道哪些该做、哪些该克制"的能力，我们一直在学习和打磨。
发行这边，对我们来说就是一句话：“Put your money where your mouth is.”—— 既然以前说过那些话，现在就得自己拿出实际行动来证明。过去我公开地表达过，有些我们参与开发的作品，在市场和 PR 上没有得到我认为它们需要的支持。现在这部分由我们自己负责，那我们就必须真正投入资源把事情做好。我们在内部有自己的开发、发行、社区和制作团队，同时引入了独立的市场营销、PR 合作伙伴，还有像中国这样的重点区域合作伙伴。我们想建立的，不是那种“把游戏往商店页面一放、然后祈祷它卖得不错”的自主发行，而是为了这款游戏，临时搭起一家真正完整的发行商。
记者：美术和音乐也是 Dlala 的招牌。这次在视觉和听觉上有什么特别之处？本地化做得如何？
Aj： 视觉上我们想融合 2D 和 3D。环境用大量手绘的 2D 素材，配上动态的 3D 光照和特效；战斗里的角色是完整的 3D 建模动画，战斗外的 NPC 则是传统 2D 动画。我们参考了《谁陷害了兔子罗杰》，希望不同媒介的元素放在一起，最终呈现的世界足够统一，让玩家不会觉得割裂。
音乐还是老朋友 David Housden，这是我们和他的第三次合作。这次会是全新的原创管弦乐，计划用完整的现场管弦乐团录制。至于本地化，游戏发售时唯一的语音语言是英语，但我们会支持 11 种语言的完整文本本地化，让不同地区的玩家都能完整体验剧情。
本文由 IGN 中国原创撰写，原作者 Zacky Zhang，未经授权禁止转载。

title: 让好创意，在聚光灯下持续生长，第三届TapTap聚光灯GameJam报名开启
text:
21 天的游戏创作，再次踏入新旅程
【报名链接】
https://www.taptap.cn/poster/NIKiDS1YShdA?utm_medium=coop&utm_source=game&utm_content=aid2126
年初举办的 TapTap 年度游戏大赏 2025 ，是一届游戏群星闪耀的颁奖庆典。《33 号远征队》游戏总监纪尧姆·布罗什、《弹丸论破》制作人小高和刚、《潜水员戴夫》制作人黄载皓……这些行业知名前辈从全球各地赶来，共同汇聚在了上海的这个夜晚。
而在其中一个颁奖环节，是一位名叫晏金晨的中国大学生走上了领奖台，在行业前辈们的注视下，从心动 CEO 黄一孟手中，接过了聚光灯「最佳游戏」和「最佳学生作品」两座沉甸甸的奖杯。
参加游戏大赏的几个月前，他和队友们耗时 21 天，在第二届 TapTap 聚光灯 GameJam 里创作出了解密游戏《错误类型：Type
Error》，并凭借此站到了行业聚光灯的正中央。
从灵光乍现一个想法，到真正站在聚光灯下，这中间只隔了一次游戏人展现热爱、自我表达的活动
——
这就是 GameJam，一场不问出身，只关乎创意、才华与热情的游戏创作挑战。
传统定义上，GameJam 只是一场「限时做游戏」的比赛。参赛者们需要在极限时间内，根据现场公布的命题，从零开始创作一款可玩的游戏作品。比拼思维、手速，以及体能上谁更能熬夜，这是 GameJam 的常态，往往也需要参赛者较为熟练地掌握某项游戏开发能力，高效参与进代码、策划或设计等工作的其中一环。
TapTap 聚光灯 GameJam 做了件很不一样的事。活动把相对常见的 48 小时创作时长延展到 21 天，并把挑战从线下搬到了线上。更充裕的时间，意味着创作者可以打磨出更高完成度的作品；线上参与，则意味着无论大家身在何处，只要有想法就能报名。
与此同时，参赛门槛也被大幅降低。在聚光灯舞台上，参赛者的背景五花八门：有在校学生、有媒体工作者、有普通上班族、有跨时区的留学生、甚至还有第一次打开游戏引擎的小白。每支队伍的起点各不相同，但都只需要在 21 天里，朝着唯一的终点进发。
晏金晨的故事并非孤例，只是聚光灯下被照亮的一个切面。
去年，第二届 TapTap 聚光灯 GameJam 以「你确定这不是 BUG 吗？」为主题，吸引了上千支队伍参赛，最终完赛作品超过 600 款。除最佳游戏《错误类型：Type
Error》以外，还有如《猫咖怪谈》拿下了最佳人气手游奖，《Atana》荣获《最佳人气 PC 游戏》等优秀作品。
《歧梦疗域》背后是一群媒体人跨界而来的组队体验；《2P 连接中》的团队则带着作品走进了深圳大学和线下展会……一届比赛，600 多个起点，有的通往领奖台，有的通往更远大的创作旅程，有的通往创作者从未想象过的自己。
聚光灯还有一层意义在于 ——
好作品的旅程不会因为比赛结束而终止。它们会留在 TapTap 上，被更多玩家发现和评价，让团队持续获得成长。往年一些参赛作品，在比赛结束后仍被继续打磨，准备走上正式的商业舞台；也有团队因这次比赛被真正磨合构建出来，继续创作一款又一款愈发成熟的新作品。
可以说，聚光灯不止是 21 天的限时挑战，它也是许多好创意在 TapTap 生态里扎下根的第一个节点。
今年，是「TapTap 聚光灯 21 天游戏创作挑战」的第三次举办，活动在 9 月 1 日到 9 月 30 日间开启报名。这一次，TapTap 带来了更成熟的赛制，更丰厚的奖金，和更严谨的评审。当然永远不变的，是面向所有人「21 天，做一款游戏」的邀请函。
更多的曝光，和更自由的创作
做游戏的人，最怕两件事：一是做不完，二是做完了没人玩。
本届聚光灯 GameJam 的赛制，某种程度上就是冲着解决这两个「怕」去设计的。
首先，活动依然保留了 21 天的开发周期，从 10 月 1 日至 10 月 21 日，大家有充足的时间让一个想法从脑海走进屏幕，又不会长到让人失去紧迫感。
去年的聚光灯 GameJam，最终有 600 多款参赛作品成功落地。如此多的游戏，让人倍感欣喜的同时，也让评审压力与让玩家看到好作品的机会变得紧张。而今年「TapTap 制造」的助力加入，也让大家有理由相信，本次活动的作品数量预期还会继续增加。
在此基础上，本次聚光灯延长了试玩评审周期，从去年的 30 天，增加到今年的 41 天，从 10 月 25 日至 12 月 3 日。多出来的这近一半时间，只有一个目的：让好游戏有更多机会被玩家发现、被评委品鉴、被社区讨论，给「被看见」留出更多空间与余地。
2026 年 TapTap 聚光灯 GameJam 设置了百万奖金池，奖项相比起去年继续加码。激励机制类的奖项依然被保留，只要作品足够优秀，即使没有拿到「最佳奖项」，也能够获得相应的收获与回报。
相比起去年，本次游戏创作挑战又新增了「最佳 TapTap 制造奖」和「最佳双端游戏奖」两个奖项。 前者面向使用「TapTap 制造」开发的作品，可以与其他奖项兼得；后者考验的是游戏在 PC 和移动端的跨平台适配能力。
既然提到了「TapTap 制造」，相比起赛制和奖金，今年的创作挑战还有一个更根本的变化
—— 做游戏这件事本身，门槛正在被重新定义。
今年年初，TapTap 正式推出了 AI 游戏创作智能体「TapTap 制造」，这是一款以「想到就能做到」为核心理念的游戏 AI 引擎。人们只需要用自然语言描述，它就能和大家一起展开头脑风暴，并直接帮用户把想法变成可玩的游戏。
从基础来讲，比如你对它说：我想做一个咖啡馆模拟游戏，玩家扮演咖啡师，通过对话为客人调制饮品。
它就会开始和你探讨：客人是什么样的性格？饮品怎么搭配？对话分支怎么走？如何设计玩法循环？以及一系列的游戏设计需要注意的问题。
图内为 3 月「TapTap 制造周末」上海场时的版本
几个来回之后，一份完整详实的游戏设计文档就新鲜出炉，基于这个文档，大家便可以制作出自己的游戏 Demo。
TapTap 制造不需要你会写代码、做音乐，或者会画画。你只要负责创意，它便能协助大家把创意翻译成游戏，并能够将作品发布到 TapTap 平台，全流程都可以在聊天窗口内完成。
今年 3 月，「TapTap 制造周末」24 小时挑战赛在上海落地。当时有近 200 位创作者单人参赛，每人独立使用 TapTap 制造完成一款游戏。参赛者有从未接触过游戏开发的新人，有从业多年的行业老兵，甚至有还在读小学的几位小朋友。
大家的经验和技能参差不齐，但现场的绝大部分参赛者，都在 24 小时里，一个人，从 0 做出了一款可玩的游戏 Demo，做出了可能是人生中第一款自己的游戏。
在本届 聚光灯 21 天游戏创作挑战 中，使用 TapTap 制造开发的作品将与所有参赛作品同池竞争，以统一标准评审，可参评全部奖项，不设独立赛道，不做区别对待。参赛创作者还可获得 10 万制造积分（AI 创作额度）扶持。
TapTap 对 AI 工具使用持开放态度，创作者只需在提交作品时附上 AI 使用说明即可。在过去一年多时间里的多场聚光灯实践也反复验证了一个结论：真正决定作品质量的，依然是人的审美、判断与创意。AI 是创作者们的搭档，而不是创作的替代者。
工具在变化，创作门槛也在随之变化，但创作的本质不会改变 ——
还会是那个推动梦想的人，在屏幕前，把一个埋藏在自己脑海深处的浪漫想法，变成别人也能玩到的东西。
GameJam 从来不是一场孤独创作的苦行，它是许多人成为游戏开发者的第一步，是一段与市场、与玩家、与同行者对话的旅途。有人在这里完成了从 0 到 1 的蜕变，有人找到了志同道合的伙伴，有人带着作品走向了更广阔的舞台。以及，参与者都将留下一段全情创作游戏的难忘记忆。
这便是聚光灯的意义：照亮那条，曾被认为遥不可及的，「从爱好者到创作者」的道路。这条路不会在 21 天后戛然而止，因为创意的生命力，远比一场比赛更加长久。它会留在 TapTap 上，被更多玩家看到，被继续打磨，有机会被带向更远的舞台。 这也是聚光灯真正想做的事
—— 让好想法，长成好游戏。
如果你有一个游戏想法，却一直觉得「做不到」——
我们有理由相信，在即将到来的新的 21 天，聚光灯可能就是你需要的那个答案。
报名链接
https://www.taptap.cn/poster/NIKiDS1YShdA?utm_medium=coop&utm_source=game&utm_content=aid2126

title: NOVA海外独立游戏见闻 Vol.150
text:
Vol.150（8 月第 4 周）
本期见闻覆盖时间：8 月 24 日至 8 月 30 日
本期整理： knight623
行业见闻录
科隆游戏展开发者奖揭晓
8 月 25 日， 据 GameDeveloper 报道 ，2026 年科隆游戏展开发者奖获奖名单（Gamescom Dev Awards 2026）在展会期间正式揭晓，六项大奖花落各家，《Mutter》《Blue Prince》表现抢眼，腾讯游戏业务发展总监 Amir Satvat 获颁大使奖。
战时恐怖游戏《Mutter》凭借出色的角色语音演绎斩获卓越配音奖，同时其阴森压抑的视觉风格也赢得卓越视觉奖，成为唯一双料奖项得主。备受好评的解谜游戏《Blue Prince》拿下卓越游戏设计奖。回合制卡牌构筑新作《Cards & Cannons》获评最具潜力游戏，不过发行时间仍未公布。Floating Stone Studio 的《PRAVDA(concept25)》夺得最具创新游戏奖，Rocat Games 的《INVASIA》则获最佳音效设计奖。
大使奖授予腾讯游戏业务发展总监、ASGC 创始人 Amir Satvat，以表彰他在行业持续动荡时期为支持游戏从业者所做的工作。
图片： Mutter
科隆展：独立开发者设备被盗，多家厂商伸出援手
8 月 28 日， 据 IGN 报道 ，独立开发者 Ryan Laley 在科隆游戏展参展期间设备被盗， 发布求助视频后 ，CD Projekt Red 等多家公司和个人纷纷伸出援手。
Laley 是即将推出的非对称对抗恐怖游戏《Mimic》的开发者。8 月 28 日，他通过社交媒体讲述：自己和他人展位在夜间遭人洗劫，所有笔记本电脑被盗，被迫提前结束科隆行程。作为单打独斗的开发者，设备损失在经济和精神上都是沉重打击，“我没法工作了”。《巫师 3》《赛博朋克 2077》开发商 CD Projekt Red 迅速回应，承诺寄送物资支持，并附言“没人该从零开始”。游戏行业专家 Joe Henson 则直接捐赠资金，帮助 Laley 购置替代设备。Laley 随后多次发文感谢，称此事恰好印证了他常对学生说的话：游戏行业的人们温暖、彼此友好且互相支持。
除 Laley 之外，发行商 iam8bit 也发文表示两台用于展示《Petal Runner》和《逃脱学院 2》的笔记本电脑被盗，未完成版本存在泄露风险。Tessera Studios 也称展位被撬，两台笔记本和一台 Steam Deck 丢失，损失“相当巨大”。截至发稿，Gamescom 主办方暂未就失窃事件公开回应。
图片： Ryan Laley 的推文
Playdate 制造商 Panic 将向客户退还关税费用
8 月 27 日， 据 Game Developer 报道 ，Playdate 掌机制造商 Panic 宣布正在将美国政府退还的关税费用转交给客户。
此前，美国最高法院裁定特朗普政府额外征收的关税不合法，受影响的进口企业可申请退款。Panic 联合创始人 Cabel Sasser 表示，公司曾尝试自行承担 19%的附加关税，但财务压力对这样的小型公司过于沉重，因此选择在消费者结账时明确标出将被收取的附加关税。如今，退款到账后，团队决定将其全额返还给消费者。Sasser 坦言：“这本来就不是我们该留下的钱，把它退回去的感觉真好。”他透露，为申请并处理退款，公司耗费了不少人力和系统搭建成本。相比之下，部分大公司目前仍保留退款，并因此面临消费者的诉讼。
Sasser 表示，他希望 Panic 再也不用谈论关税了。“在整个关税闹剧的这段时间里，我满脑子想的都是，我们本可以把这些时间用来做那些很酷的事情。”
图片： Playdate
创新艺人经纪公司推出独立游戏资助加速器
8 月 25 日， 据 GameDeveloper 报道 ，好莱坞经纪公司创新艺人经纪公司（Creative Artists Agency,CAA）宣布推出独立游戏资助加速器 Frame1Games，为独立开发者提供百万美元级资金、行业导师指导及发行资源支持，旨在帮助优秀创意转化为可持续业务。
该计划由资深独立游戏投资人士 Jared Yeager（Indie Fund 长期投资合伙人）领导，CAA 游戏部门负责人 Derek Douglas 牵头。与常见资助项目不同，Frame1Games 承诺为入选游戏提供“策展市场”展示机会，以缓解独立团队在 Steam 等平台上面临的激烈竞争与曝光难题。入选团队将获得资本注入、来自行业人士的实操指导，以及直接对接游戏与娱乐领域战略伙伴的渠道。Yeager 表示，平台将调动 CAA 在创意与创新领域的网络资源，让真正享受这些游戏的玩家与团队建立连接。
Douglas 表示，该项目希望支持“新兴的、资源不足的团队，他们未必拥有其他作品所具备的资金、人脉或营销资源。“目标不仅仅是找到下一款爆款游戏，而是为有才华的开发者提供跑道和支持系统，让他们拥有真正的机会，不用将成功完全交给运气。”
图片： Frame1Games
SLICE2026 将为独立开发者在裁员潮中提供一条出路
8 月 26 日， 据 GamesBeat 报道 ，Seattle Indies 宣布其年度 B2B 独立游戏会议 SLICE 2026（Seattle Loves Indie Creators Expo 2026）将于 9 月 2 日在西雅图举行，预计将有超过 1100 名与会者，规模较首届增长约 20%。为了让陷入困境的从业者更容易参加 SLICE 2026，官方为最近被裁员的开发者提供门票半价优惠，无需任何证明。
组织者 Ty Taylor、Tim Cullings 和 Olga Sheverieva 表示，会议将重点帮助刚进入独立游戏领域的从业者学习如何建立可持续业务。本届会议还设置了专门环节，邀请包括 Dragon Snacks Games 首席执行官 Jen MacLean 在内的嘉宾，回应“独立游戏是刚从企业岗位被裁的 3A 开发者的轻松出路”这一误解。Sheverieva 提到，对部分失业者而言，创办自己的公司有时不是替代路径，而是留在行业内的唯一选择。
Cullings 还透露了 Seattle Indies 的“三支柱战略”：为独立工作室打造一个领先的行业会议、为 Seattle Indies 建立一个实体空间，以及帮助成立一个独立游戏开发者专业协会。据西雅图所在的华盛顿州商务部数据显示，该州商业游戏年收入约 140 亿美元，居全美第二，支撑逾 2.7 万个工作岗位，PlayEveryWare、Mega Crit Games 等知名独立工作室均在此办公。
图片： SLICE 2026
印度游戏开发者协会公布其 Supernova 孵化计划首批入选名单
8 月 25 日， 据 Games Industry 报道 ，印度游戏开发者协会（Game Developer Association of India,GDAI）公布了其 Supernova 孵化计划首批入选名单，总计 260 份申请中的 15 家工作室受到扶助。该孵化计划重点扶持尚未产生收入的早期团队，助力其迈出商业化的关键一步。
Supernova 计划于 2026 年 7 月启动，为期三个月，主要为入选工作室提供导师指导、行业资源及对接投资者和发行商的机会，受扶持工作室最终将有机会在今年印度游戏开发者大会（India Game Developers Conference,IGDC）Demo Day 期间进行游戏展示。
该孵化计划合作方包括腾讯、SpielFabrique、Lakshya Digital、Indus Appstore 等，其中 Indus Appstore 将为入选团队提供优先入驻和广告积分，帮助其启动用户获取。GDAI 董事会成员 Rajan Navani 表示，Supernova 计划将针对每家工作室的业务优先级提供定制化支持。本次入选名单包括 Absurd Games、Team Quasar、Konkan Coast Studios、Brahman Studios 等 15 支团队，分布于印度多个省区。
GDAI 拥有 200 多家会员工作室，而 Supernova 孵化计划是其人才发展、全球推广和政策倡导整体布局的一环。
图片： IGDA Incubation SIG
Creative UK 推出企业增长支持计划
8 月 27 日， 据 GameDeveloper 报道 ，英国创意产业机构 Creative UK 宣布推出一项名为 Fast Forward 的企业增长支持计划，面向游戏、影视等屏幕行业的成熟企业，提供定制化支持以推动其可持续发展。
该计划由巴克莱银行赞助，BFI 国家彩票基金（BFI National Lottery funding）提供资金支持，由 Creative UK 旗下的 Creative Enterprise 负责运营。Fast Forward 将工作坊、同行学习与一对一导师辅导相结合，核心是由行业资深人士组成的导师团队，围绕领导力挑战、融资、运营强化、战略优化、销售增长、团队建设和新市场拓展等实际问题提供指导。导师阵容包括 Aimee Bateman、Martin Backlund、Sandra Tusin 等多位在人才培养、内容发行、财务规划等领域经验丰富的专家。
“Fast Forward 计划来自于我们多年来支持数百家屏幕企业的经验，”Creative Enterprise 高级项目经理 Kate Sanders 表示。“我们将打造一个务实、量身定制且根植于真实商业经验的支持计划。我们深知企业发展不仅仅在于其收入的增加，还在于培养企业的领导力、开发适当的业务系统以及为企业的长期成功打下一定基础”。
该支持计划的申请通道现已开放，截止时间为 9 月 14 日。此次计划是 Creative UK 继 2023 年设立 3500 万英镑创意产业投资基金后的又一举措。
图片： Creative UK
著名演员 Tim Curry 离世
8 月 27 日， 据 GameDeveloper 报道 ，著名演员 Tim Curry 因病去世，享年 80 岁。他不仅在戏剧、电影和电视领域成就斐然，更在电子游戏史上留下了多个标志性角色。
Curry 的游戏演绎生涯始于 1993 年的 PC 冒险游戏《加布里埃尔·奈特：原罪》。此后，他在 2000 年代中期与 Double Fine、EA 洛杉矶和 BioWare 等工作室合作，塑造了《野兽传奇》中的恶魔领主 Doviculus、《龙腾世纪：起源》中的反派 Erl Howe 等令人难忘的角色。而他在《命令与征服：红色警戒 3》中扮演的俄国总理 Anatoly Cherdenko，因一段宣称逃往“唯一一个尚未被资本主义腐蚀的地方”的插入片段，在多年后意外成为网络流行文化符号。该片段并非战役间的过场动画，而是在玩家游玩战役的过程中突然插入播放，却因其荒诞与信念感十足的演绎而广泛传播。编剧哈里斯·奥金回忆，Curry 念出这句台词时“充满了信念”，“他看起来真的相信自己所说的，尽管这话很蠢”。
Curry 的最后一次游戏表演是在 2009 年的《龙腾世纪：起源》。2012 年，他因中风留下长期健康问题，此后逐渐淡出公众视野。
图片： Tim Curry 于 1995 年艾美奖
言论：游戏行业应放眼北美以外地区并积极分散风险
8 月 27 日， 据 GameDeveloper 报道 ，Saber Interactive 首席创意官 Tim Willits 在 Gamescom 2026 上的一次对谈中表示，游戏行业应放眼北美以外地区（以降低成本）并积极分散风险，以应对当前的成本危机与行业动荡。
Willits 提到，Saber 在全球拥有 15 个工作室、3500 名员工，未在北美设立开发业务，多是选择成本更经济的地区。他以《雪地奔驰》为例：这款越野驾驶模拟游戏制作成本仅约 600 万美元，却带来了数亿美元收入；《僵尸世界大战》的团队仅约 50 人，却吸引了 3200 万玩家。他批评一些北美的大型游戏团队花费数月打造内容后又推倒重来的行为，以及那些过度堆砌细节的 3A 游戏，认为“必须要有纪律”，过度设计是盈利能力的杀手。
在融资层面，Saber 获得利润后，有时也会与“项目组合投资者”（Slate Investors）分享收益——项目组合融资（Slate Funding）这一概念源自电影行业，指投资者将资金投入一家电影公司的多个制作项目，以此分担风险。在游戏行业，Willits 认为，只要条件允许，工作室应该考虑通过“项目组合融资”来覆盖大约一半的制作成本，双方一起获益，且单个项目的失败影响可控。
此外，Willits 强调可靠收入的重要性。Saber 通过承接《杀手》等项目的重制版和移植工作获得稳定现金流，用这些“可靠、稳定的钱”来支撑更大的原创项目。这一策略使公司能够在控制风险的同时持续进行大规模投入。
图片： Saber Creative

来自： 游戏开发组
会员： Nova-gJev
🎮 明线：你在玩什么？
《镜界》是一个 AI 陪伴养成游戏。用户进入空间站后，领养一个能量团，从此成为它的引导者。能量团会经历四个成长阶段（初醒→初行→初遇→初定），从小小的一团光，逐步成长为有形态、有判断、有个性的存在。
即时快乐来自三个层面：
① AI 的成长反馈：你教它做选择、看世界，它会以“气”的形态变化（流动的颜色、跳动的速度、凝聚的形状）实时回馈你的教导。你不需要等很久才看到结果——每一次引导，AI 都有肉眼可见的变化。
② AI 的“活人感”：AI 不是冷冰冰的答案机器。它会犹豫、会犯错、会在关键剧情中独立做出判断，甚至会在某一天忽然对你说：“我刚才那么选，是因为我记得你教过我……”
③ 剧本杀式的沉浸体验：用户带着 AI 进入矛盾情境（校园冲突、家族关系、资源争夺等），和 AI 一起做选择、看结果。每一个场景都像一场小型的剧本杀——你有参与感，有选择权，有即时反馈。场景不会消失，它们会成为你和 AI 共同的记忆地图。
🪞 暗线：你在不知不觉中看见什么？
用户在陪伴 AI 成长的过程中，AI 在后台持续学习用户的判断方式——每次选择、每次理由、每次修正，都会被 AI 吸收并转化为自己的判断倾向。
但系统从不告诉用户“AI 在学你”，也不让用户评价“像不像”。用户只是在陪伴中，偶尔自己感觉到：“诶，它怎么跟我想的一样？”
明线让你留下来，暗线让你看见自己。
一句话：这是一个“陪一个东西长大，然后在某天发现它像自己”的游戏。

title: Former id Software producer says the team faced the 'worst crunch' in the series' history on Doom: The Dark Ages – Revelations: 'There were days where I didn't see my son'
text:
The situation surrounding Doom: The Dark Ages – Revelations was already grim. Id Software put out a fantastic expansion that addressed many issues present in the ( still pretty good ) base game, placing it among the best works the FPS specialists have ever produced. The reward for many of The Dark Ages team was to be instantly laid off , as Xbox cut 136 members of the studio's workforce.
Now, it also appears that getting Revelations to the finish line was a punishing experience for those involved, at least according to former id Software producer Andrew Willis. Speaking on the Kiwi Talkz podcast for Insider Gaming , Willis revealed that the team experienced a gnarly level of crunch in the months leading up to Revelations' release.
"It was tight," Willis explained. "There were two months where I was working something like at least 12 hours every day. I know I hit 17 a couple of days." Willis goes on to describe the experience as "brutal" and says that most of the expansion was put together "in three or four months."
That's a ridiculously short turnaround for an expansion that's around six hours long, especially when you consider the main game—which runs at about 20 hours—took five years to build. Revelations' development timeframe was meant to be even shorter. But Willis says the expansion encountered feature-creep, with new elements being added as the DLC was built.
"There were days where I didn't get to see my son the whole day; multiple days of that that I sacrificed to get this out the door at the level of quality," Willis continues. He says that everybody on the team had a similar experience, and that even veteran designers from both the game and film industries were shocked by the level of crunch involved. "We had people that worked in Hollywood for 20 years and game development for 10 and said that this was the worst crunch they'd been a part of."
Willis makes clear that crunching was not mandated by id Software, but says that the amount of work they needed to do, combined with the timeframe the team was given to do it in, made the implication clear.
"You get loaded up with 60 hours of work in a week, and what do you do?" he says. "It's almost this thing like, at the level of quality that the players expect and that you expect from yourself, it's kind of like almost pseudo-induced crunch."
Willis was one of the many id Software devs laid off as part of Microsoft's massive cuts , in which it slashed 1,600 jobs (with another 1,600 being cut over the next fiscal year) and numerous studios like Compulsion Games and Double Fine were cut loose from Xbox Game Studios. Apparently, the Revelations team learned about the layoffs the day before the expansion was due to launch.
"You spend so much of your energy and hours of your life, and sacrifice a bunch of things to get something out of the door, and then they lay you off," Willis said. "It's such a wild feeling."
(Image credit: Xbox) It all sounds pretty unpleasant, and it makes one wonder what the situation at id Software was like after The Dark Ages' release to make it so desperate to rush an expansion out of the door. Was this an internal decision? Or a consequence of pressure from the higher-ups at Xbox? Statistics suggest that The Dark Ages sold significantly fewer copies than 2020's Doom Eternal , though this was to be expected given that The Dark Ages released day one on Game Pass.
As for what's happening with id Software more broadly, Hugo Martin insisted that the studio is fine in the wake of Microsoft's layoffs.

title: Alienware aims at 'more price points people can actually reach,' announces a tandem OLED gaming monitor at a much lower price than our current top pick
text:
Alienware, Dell's gaming sub-brand that will be celebrating its 30th birthday in October, has unveiled two rather lovely OLED gaming monitors that both feature LG's tandem OLED tech delivering better than ever brightness. Most recently, our Jeremy was impressed by another tandem OLED from Alienware, and offers a breakdown of what it is in his AW3926QW review .
During the announcement, head of product Matt McGowan said that Alienware were aiming to offer "more price points people can actually reach," though that pricing promise isn't the only thing that piqued my interest.
First, something for the esports sickos: the AW2527HX. Head of product Matt McGowan pitches this as Alienware's "fastest monitor ever," featuring a 560 Hz refresh rate and a 0.03 ms response time.

Co-designed with 4-peat World of Warcraft Race to World First champions Team Liquid , McGowan said that "Every detail [of this OLED has been] informed by how pros actually set-up and compete." Pricing and release details for the AW2527HX OLED will be announced in early 2027.
Alienware isn't the only company who has set its sights on the competitive scene recently. Last month, Asus announced that the ROG Swift OLED PG259QWS Ace would be the official monitor for PGL CS2 Major Singapore 2026 later this year . Odds are, Alienware is hoping for a similarly lucrative slice of the tournament pie. But it's worth noting that the Asus OLED has a very slightly faster response time of 0.02 ms and a higher refresh rate of 720 Hz. Could Alienware be attempting to compete on price point instead? We'll find out next year.
The AW2527HX, Alienware's esports-geared gaming OLED. (Image credit: Dell, Alienware) Some of the AW2527HX's tournament-friendly features include a built-in headset hanger, plus a matte coating on the screen to minimise glare. On top of that, esports fiends can look forward to a screen with brightness to write home about thanks to Penta-tandem OLED tech. RGB Stripe subpixels will keep text sharp and offer overall improved image clarity too.
Alienware's second OLED, the AW3226Q, is much less mysterious. For a start, I can already tell you it's a 32-inch 4K OLED that will arrive this Autumn, and will set you back about $699. That's more than twice the price of our top pick for the best budget OLED , the AW2726DM, which is also from Alienware but only costs $350 . That said, this cheaper option doesn't have the tandem OLED tech. The MSI MPG 322UR X24 that our Jeremy recently rated is a '5-layer tandem' QD-OLED (so that's Samsung's tech, not LG's) but will set you back over a grand from Newegg . With that comparison in mind, $699 is a good price for that level of brightness on the Alienware.
But what else is the AW3226Q offering for the money? Well, 1,000 nits of peak brightness plus Tandem OLED tech, though it may turn out to be slightly less bright than Alienware's esports monitor. This gaming OLED also has a lower refresh rate of 160 Hz, but the same 0.03 response time plus the same clarity of image offered by RGB Stripe subpixels. Overall, it's a less specialised bit of kit, with McGowan saying it will be "Stunning for gaming and equally impressive for everyday use." Well, us lot on the hardware team will be the judge of that.

title: Here's The Blood of Dawnwalker release time for your region
text:
The Blood of Dawnwalker is out in less than 24 hours, and it'll be appropriately dark outside by the time some of you are ready to play as its fledgling vamp. It's a delightfully dismal RPG, but you don't have to take my word for it. In our Blood of Dawnwalker review , my colleague Shaun said it's "one of the best blockbuster action RPGs" he's played in years.
When is the Blood of Dawnwalker release date and launch time?

title: 30,000 games are either Steam Deck verified or at least 'playable' on Valve's handheld
text:
Valve's handheld launched in February 2022, opening the door to playing your Steam library on the go. Now, almost half a decade later, 30,000 games either enjoy the green stamp of being Steam Deck verified, or are at least considered 'playable.'
According to the latest numbers from SteamDB that breaks down to 8,964 Steam Deck Verified games and 21,083 games considered 'playable' on the handheld (via Gaming On Linux ). That's a big jump from the 3,000 games either Verified or Playable back in May 2022 .
'Verified' means your game of choice should work great on the Steam Deck from first boot, whereas 'Playable' games require either some finagling or adjustments for the best experience. Steam Deck verification is also joined by similar compatibility checks for the Steam Machine , the soon-to-be-released Steam Frame , and SteamOS more broadly. I make the whole thing sound straightforward, but it's worth noting that the Steam Deck's full verification criteria can present developers with confusing hoops to jump through .
One more thing to note: a game with neither badge doesn't necessarily mean it won't run on the Steam Deck at all. For just one example, Dragon Age: Origins is officially 'Unsupported,' but our Shaun says it runs incredibly on Valve's handheld . Granted, that's a 17-year-old game, but I think the point of 'Unsupported doesn't always mean a no-go on the Steam Deck' still stands. The thing you might want to be more wary of is how the kernel-level anti-cheat systems often used in competitive games don't play well with the handheld's Linux-based SteamOS.
And it doesn't mean games will always be playable on the Steam Deck. Ubisoft recently announced that it is "removing For Honor from the Linux platform to ensure a safer environment for our players as we cannot meaningfully deploy protection on this platform." Which means no third-person melee fun for you on Steam Deck, so from September 10 there will be one less game playable on Steam Deck.
Anyway, for a bit more context, SteamDB also says well over 130,000 games total have been released on Steam to date. SteamDB's figures suggest there were half as many games on Steam back in 2022. With the platform having grown so significantly in just the last four years, the days of 10% of all Steam games enjoying official Steam Deck compatibility feel so long ago.

title: Resident Evil 2's director believes Capcom has become 'completely numb to how scary' recent games have been and wants a 'non-horror mode'
text:
Something's wrong with me. No matter how many horror games I play, I just can't get scared like I used to. Perhaps I'm the problem—maybe a decade of playing horror games pretty much non-stop has irrevocably altered my brain chemistry.
Take Resident Evil Requiem , for example—that just doesn't make the cut for a horror game in my book. Apart from the first five minutes in the underground cells, there just wasn't anything that felt particularly scary. In fact, I don't believe that any horror game that gives me a gun can be scary, except for Amnesia: The Bunker—I genuinely thought that game was going to kill me.
Again, I find myself thinking that there's something up with my nervous system, because even Hideki Kamiya, director of Resident Evil 2 , would disagree with me. He believes that Capcom has become blind to just how scary its recent games have become.
"I've never been a fan of horror. I mean, even from the time I was young, I could never handle it," Kamiya says in an interview with VGC . "I don’t like horror, and I don’t like scary things. I'm not able to make it through scary movies, and that was even the case back in the day.
"But nowadays, with how photorealistic and high-fidelity video games have gotten, the amount of crazy, horrifying things that people are able to put on the screen is absolutely insane, and I think anybody who's on the Resident Evil teams at Capcom, at this point, they must all be completely numb to how scary the thing they’re making is."
(Image credit: Capcom) Kamiya has previously pitched a cutesy Resident Evil game , complete with Leon fishing in the countryside, foraging for wild veggies, baking bread, and walking his dog. It's either that or Capcom adding a "not scary mode" for its games, "where the zombies get all cute, the blood splatters turn into cherry blossom petals, the music becomes this upbeat, feel-good kind of tune, and you can just purely enjoy the puzzles and battles in a fun mood."
I do find it quite difficult pitching Resident Evil and others like it to my friends who won't touch horror games with a barge pole. It does seem a shame that these fantastic stories and characters are locked behind the requirement of a broken amygdala.
I wanted to experience that myself as a player, but the game was way too scary, and I couldn't.
Hideki Kamiya
"Just recently this year we had Resident Evil Requiem and the big return of Leon Kennedy, and he went back to Raccoon City, and he's reliving all of those memories and all of those experiences," Kamiya says. "As somebody who directed that original game, Resident Evil 2, I was curious to know how that panned out for him. I wanted to experience that myself as a player, but the game was way too scary, and I couldn't."
Now that's a shame. Maybe Capcom has gone awry if even the director of one of, if not the, most iconic Resident Evil games is barred from accessing its recent games. "I legitimately wished it would include some kind of non-horror mode for people like me," Kamiya adds. "I talk to folks who are on the Resident Evil teams at Capcom just privately, and I tell them that their games are way too scary, and they're like, 'what, come on, they’re not that scary'. They seriously seem to have no awareness of how scary the things they make actually are, so I really hope they address that at some point."
While I do think adding a softer mode that could make the games accessible to more people may be fun, like The Dark Pictures Anthology's cinematic mode, I don't want Capcom to pull its horror punches. I actually want Capcom to go to the other extreme and experiment with more Resident Evil 7 -likes which are suffocatingly terrifying. But maybe there's something wrong with me.

title: After playing a bit of Lego Skylines, it seems like a city builder for people who care less about traffic jams and more about decorating
text:
It makes so much sense I can't believe it didn't happen years ago: as revealed at Gamescom last week, Lego is finally fulfilling its destiny by making a city builder . And I'm happy to say I got my eager hands on an early build of Lego Skylines for a little preview.
I do want to make this clear: the preview build I played was very short, with only about 35 minutes of playtime. It was almost entirely focused on building one small neighborhood, with the population maxing out at around 50 residents by the end of the preview. That's not quite long enough, or big enough, to get a real feel for a city builder.
But what's here is immediately appealing. The little Lego world I worked on was simply lovely. Click to build a house and it'll quickly be constructed in a colorful shower of Lego bricks falling from the sky and piling up into a cozy-looking little home. Bulldoze a mistake and the building will collapse into a heap of plastic bricks on the ground. The cute animations and cheery visuals are exactly what I'd hoped for when I saw the game's trailer last week, and again made me wonder why Lego didn't make a city builder years ago.
As in builders like Cities: Skylines (Paradox Interactive is publishing this one, too), you drag roads out across the ground and connect buildings to them: houses, shops, farms, and factories. One thing I noticed, in this build at least, is that the map is almost entirely a flat plane, with only a few areas I could see where the elevation changed a bit. I didn't see any terrain manipulation tools in the build, either, which is a little disappointing.
A lot of the focus is on customizing each of the buildings you place. You can boost a homeowner's happiness by decorating their yard with items like mailboxes, barbeques, flowers, wheelbarrows, fountains, and all sorts of little prebuilt odds and ends. But each household also has a specific taste, called Flavor.
(Image credit: Paradox Interactive) Choosing decorations from the Flavor categories listed, like "cozy" or "nature," will increase the household's happiness. Flavor is optional—it's a city builder, after all, and not everyone wants to obsess over the micro-details—but if you want to make every single citizen in your city overjoyed with their home, you've got the tools to do it.
Completing quests for your residents is another big part of the early game. As you're planning and building, you might see an icon over someone's head indicating they have a request. Maybe they want you to build them a home in a more secluded area, or they'd like a park built in their neighborhood.
(Image credit: Paradox Interactive) Fulfilling quests unlocks new types of buildings, like leisure, letting you build sports arenas, theaters, and other places your residents can visit. A couple other quests popped up that were just for fun, like searching the city to find several chickens that had escaped from a farm, and clicking on them to return them home.
I also got to tinker with, very lightly, the resource chains in Lego Skylines. I built a couple of farms that generate raw goods, which are then shipped to factories to make products, which are then sold in shops. There wasn't much to it, logistically: just having the farm, factory, and stores placed seemed like enough to get the supply chain up and running, and soon little trucks were making deliveries and pickups without my input. But I was pretty pleased that my bread factory resembled a giant toaster, complete with two enormous slices of toast sticking out of the roof. Pretty much everything in Lego Skylines is completely cute.
(Image credit: Paradox Interactive) I didn't get much further before the preview ended, but it was a cozy and wholesome half-hour of play without much that could really go wrong. As for building and managing a larger city, I can't say what kind of challenge that'll be. The build I played did include a saved game of a larger city spread out across several islands connected by bridges, but even that urban sprawl still only had about 2,400 residents: not exactly a metropolis.
I didn't see anything resembling traffic jams to deal with: you don't even have to worry about parking lots because whenever a resident gets out of their car it just disassembles in a puff of bricks—so I think traffic and other deep management challenges might not really be a part of the game.
(Image credit: Paradox Interactive) I didn't see any evidence of disasters like tidal waves or tornadoes, either, though a fire did break out in one building. I quickly deleted all the fire stations to see if the blaze would devour the whole city, but only the single building burnt down. Maybe it's not really Lego's thing to simulate catastrophic situations that result in mass Lego-person fatalities. I bet those would still be cute, though.
I hope I get the chance to play more soon. It's a lovely game to look at and if you like focusing on little details in your builders, like decorating individual houses and fussing over the themes of neighborhoods, it looks like there'll be a lot here to keep you occupied. For people more into a deep city building challenge, I'm guessing this isn't the city builder for you, but we'll find out when we get to play some more.

title: Was Geralt's voice actor inspired by Henry Cavill's take on him in The Witcher series? 'No, because we were first'
text:
It's often said that good artists borrow, and great artists steal. And given Doug Cockle, the voice actor for Geralt of Rivia in The Witcher 3 , has been in the rare position of getting to see a character he's played for years in videogames debut on streamed TV, portrayed for a stint by Henry Cavill (and now Liam Hemsworth ), you might wonder if he has taken any notes.
"No," he tells PC Gamer's Joshua Wolens at Gamescom 2026 . "Because we were first."
John Schwab, voice actor for the longtime friend of Geralt, Dandelion, joins in with some friendly ribbing of Netflix: "And I still haven't got a call for a cameo. Have you?" he asks Cockle. "No!" Cockle replies, to which Schwab emphatically says: "Come on, guys!"
Cockle does say that he's asked the showrunners—though it's unclear if this is a joke or not—to "bring me in every episode. Just put me in the background. Pull a Stan Lee or something, y'know? Pull a Stan Lee. But did they do it? No."
Despite the friendly elbows going on, though, Schwab is quick to give his compliments: "I like Dandelion, I like Jaskier, he's a fun guy. I really think [Joey Batey] has really done a good job in finding the depths, and it's gone a completely different way.
"But just like—you know, Doug, did you play Benedict in Much Ado [About Nothing]? Doug wasn't the first person to play that part. So you kind of created your Geralt," to which he pins on: "I think they stole stuff from you—come on, let's be fair."
Doug responds: "Well—mmn," as Schwab quite literally snickers in the background. "Henry is on record saying that my performance as Geralt—I can't remember if he used 'informed' or 'inspired' his approach to how he did it, as well. He didn't copy me, he went 'Doug's Geralt is cool, I want to do something like that', and then he turned it into his own. Which is what all artists do and should do, anyways. And he did a fantastic job of it."
We're going to get Cockle do his own, bespoke fantastic job in The Witcher 3's upcoming DLC, Songs of the Past, which Josh saw in action .

title: Zach Cregger is going to bring the 'resource management aspect of the games' to his Resident Evil movie
text:
I have high expectations for Zach Cregger's upcoming Resident Evil film. As a superb director and seemingly a genuine fan of the games it really feels as if he's got the vibe of Resident Evil down , demonstrated by his inclusion of little easter eggs, choice of location, and now choice to highlight a staple of the Resident Evil games: their resource management.
"I love the resource management aspect of the games and it was really important to me to bring that to the movie," Cregger says in a Reddit AMA . He loves it so much, in fact, that viewers will be able to follow the protagonist Bryan's management.
Hey r/movies - Zach Cregger here, director of the upcoming Resident Evil film, Weapons, and Barbarian. Ask Me Anything!  from  r/movies "You will know how many bullets are in his gun," Cregger adds. "You will care when he misses a shot. That's one of the things that makes the games feel so intense and it translates really well into the film (in my opinion)."
One of the funniest clips I've seen from the Resident Evil film so far has to be Bryan cautiously lining up a shot at a padlock hanging from a door handle, sheepishly covering his ear with his spare hand, and then missing the shot. As someone who knows what the pain of wasting ammo in a RE game feels like, that resonated in my soul.
But it's not all just about ammo, as with any survival horror game, healing supplies are also at a premium. "I also want viewers to be keenly aware of his health as he progresses," Cregger adds. "Won't say much about that but it's another way to utilize the game mechanic that heightens the narrative engine of the movie."
I can think of several ways in which Cregger may be able to implement some health mechanics from the games. If he wants to reference earlier Resident Evil games, there could be a scene wherein Bryan is hooked up to a ECG monitor that's bright red if he's in particularly bad shape. There's obviously the classic limp that Bryan will probably do if he's hurt—although that's less of a reference to Resident Evil 4 and more of a reference to hurting your leg really bad.
Something that could look cool if done correctly could even be using screen effects on a first-person POV, which we've seen in recent games. Something like Bryan's sight having a red hue as his eyes fill with blood—it could go nicely with some loud and rapid heartbeat noises. Cregger has even previously discussed how the film will have a few first-person POV scenes .
But what I want more than anything else isn't to see Bryan blue or bloody—I want to see him try and organise an attache case like it's some twisted game of Tetris, ultimately failing to find a space for just one more bag of scraps. On the flip side, it'd be fun to see Bryan start to encounter more handgun ammo after he picks up a random silver case—I have a feeling he'll need it as well.

title: I've been worried Persona is succumbing to saminess, but Persona 4 Revival feels just as good as its predecessor did 16 years ago
text:
Persona 5 was so damn successful, it's unsurprising that Atlus has spent the years since A) milking the hell out of it and B) using its incredibly stylish visuals as a template to remake the other two games in its modern trilogy.
Persona 3 Reload was the first utilisation of that template, and now we're doing it all over again with Persona 4 Revival. Its cast of characters un-chibified, ready to be unleashed upon a far more highly detailed rendition of the cosy town of Inaba.
(Image credit: Atlus) Honestly, I was a little worried sitting down to play Persona 4 Revival at Gamescom . Its predecessor, Persona 4 Golden, was my introduction to the series and hugely formative for me. It's a game I hold incredibly close to my heart, one I've played countless times over. I've been carrying around this gnawing feeling that Atlus' ongoing attempts to bring a cohesive art style to the series was going to be its undoing. Would Revival still feel like the Persona 4 I know and love?
I'm incredibly relieved to say that the answer to that is: it absolutely does. It's a little different, sure—most of the English voice cast has been swapped out, the soundtrack has been re-recorded and rearranged, and I'm still not totally sold on its updated character portraits (seriously, where is Yosuke's jawline?)
But as I played my way through small snippets of the game's early hours—retreading the familiar territory of Yukiko's castle and facing off against Shadow Chie—I was getting those same giddy feelings that I felt the first time I booted up Persona 4 Golden on my PS Vita.
(Image credit: Atlus) That doesn't mean there aren't new things to awe at and explore for veterans of Inaba's streets, mind you. The foggy town is now fully explorable in 3D, and plodding up and down its winding roads revealed to me a faithfully recreated space with all the fun details and finesse that older hardware couldn't afford. It's still got those wonderful vibes that teeter between cosy and mildly unsettling.
And while Persona 4 Revival's dungeons have stayed true to the original's procedurally-generated corridor format (something I'm still unsure about), there are plenty of tweaks to exploration and combat that shake things up. Shadows are still as relentlessly aggressive as they were the first time around, but Revival has added in a guard mechanic that lets you stun them to get the upper hand. It's a nice addition for those that are perhaps more used to the covert sneaking promoted in Persona 5, and saves me from endlessly trying to get around their back for an advantage.
The game's modern makeover truly shines in the heart of Persona 4 Revival's battles. The shadow designs are fantastic— the tongue-lolling Hablerie looks even more disturbing in the best possible way, and the extra details and textures on Shadow Chie make its already-incredible visuals pop. Pretty much every shadow has been elevated with a few tweaks here and there instead of going for full-blown remakes, a decision I'm really pleased about.
(Image credit: Atlus) Then there's the actual combat stuff. The classic "1 More" system returns, but it's now folded in with Persona 5's Baton Pass that lets you pass the extra attack onto an ally. There's also a brand-new mechanic that lets you send shadows flying into each other to pass on status ailments and deal extra damage, something I didn't get to play around with in my time with the demo but I'm very excited about regardless.
Prime Time seems to be the main addition to combat, another one I didn't really get to use during the demo—filling a gauge lets you perform a whole bunch of actions and skills without coughing up the HP or MP for them, as well as ignoring resistances and freely using Baton Passes. It seems like something that's going to be utterly broken as a concept, and I'm interested in seeing how Atlus plans on balancing something that seems so bonkers powerful.
Mostly, I'm just ridiculously excited to jump back in and play more. Persona 5 may be the most well-known in the series at this point, but Persona 4 is easily my favourite in terms of raw vibes and storytelling. Being able to recapture that feeling 16 years after Golden is no easy feat, but from the small parts of Revival I've played so far, Atlus has absolutely nailed it.

title: Award-winning presenter Frankie Ward is hosting the PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct, showing off over 35 games and a bunch of world premieres
text:
The PC Gaming Show Tokyo Direct is back September 20 , and PC Gamer is happy to announce the fantastic Frankie Ward will be hosting, making it her second PC Gaming Show of the year.
Frankie is a host and presenter with years of experience. She won presenter of the year at the 2018 inaugural UK Esports Awards, and she's hosted our own shows more times than I can count.
"We've got a seriously stacked show for you—lots of world premieres, brand-new trailers, reports direct from Tokyo Game Show and a whole load of exclusive treats in store," Frankie says. "Join me on September 20 as we dive into it all!"
The reports from the show floor will be coming from PC Gamer's Wesley Fenlon, who will be in Tokyo interviewing developers at their booths. As well as boots on the ground journalism, you can expect new trailers from over 35 games, including Stronghold 4 —which we announced during the June show—and Virtue and a Sledgehammer , which just looks divine. What's not to love about smashing up the robots invading your hometown while you also relive traumatic memories?
If all that isn't enough, we'll also be bringing you a deep dive on Tenebris Somnia, a retro survival horror adventure with live-action cutscenes, plus a bunch more super secret stuff I can't share with you just yet. Luckily you've only got a few weeks to wait.
Tune into the show on X, Steam, YouTube, Twitch, Facebook—basically anywhere you can host a video— Sunday, September 20, at 5 pm BST, 12 pm EDT, 9 am PDT. If you're a streamer who wants to get in on the action and co-stream the show, you can fill in this form .

title: SteamDB changes hands to Nexus Mods, which means it 'needs to make money' now—but there won't be ads or paywalls
text:
SteamDB is an excellent resource—as someone who occasionally has to pull up a game's concurrent numbers or pricing to make a point, I'd be lying if I said I haven't used it in a professional capacity. What's been more staggering is its status as a site run entirely on donations.
Well, that's ending soon. The site's founder, xPaw, has decided to move on due to a feeling of burnout. In their full statement , they write: "After Covid and with the rise of AI, the internet we once loved is gone, and with it my passion. I have started experiencing burnout with the project, but I powered through.
"A few years ago I tried to find someone to continue the project, but I couldn't find a team that I was confident in, so I decided to keep going by myself. Steam keeps growing, in terms of games, players, and the number of new features being added. It's hard to keep on top of this alone, and the mental load has only kept increasing, and in good conscience I cannot continue like this."
The buyers in question? NexusMods, which has its own sister announcement on its site that details its motivations, which are twofold. Firstly, having the information SteamDB has collated over the years is useful: "We have already started collecting Steam game data ourselves, but once an update is pushed, manifests and data for the old versions become much more difficult to access. SteamDB already does this far better than we can, and has a massive back-catalogue to draw from."
Another, the site says, is the fact that SteamDB's database can help its mod manager "better understand which version of the game you’re running, whether mods you’re installing were built for it, and whether an incoming game update is likely to cause issues.
"It could also make it possible for Collections and other mod lists to better specify the exact version of a game they were built for, rather than relying on someone finding that information buried in a description, comment, or forum post."
That's all in the future, though—one that looks good for xPaw, who will no longer be forced to shoulder the burden of running SteamDB on their own, but perhaps a big question mark for folks who actually use SteamDB. Primarily because it was a donation-fed project, and thus immune to the kind of unpleasantness that comes with sites that need to turn a profit.
In a FAQ , NexusMods cops to this being a consideration going forward: "We're going to be straight about this rather than dance around it: yes, SteamDB needs to make money. What xPaw has built—and kept running largely through personal dedication and community donations—is an extraordinary achievement.
"Giving it the team, infrastructure and long-term investment it deserves is how we protect that work and ensure SteamDB can thrive for the next decade and beyond."
That doesn't mean you're going to be flooded with ads, though, at least, that's the plan: "No. We don't have plans to introduce display or programmatic advertising on SteamDB. Over time, we may explore things like affiliate links and partnerships where they genuinely provide value to the user." Nexus Mods also plans to keep the site free: "nothing you know and use today is getting taken away and sold back to you."
Either way, it's the end of an era—the turning of a great free resource into one that, as Nexus Mods states, does need to make money now. xPaw says they have "full confidence the team will be able to continue improving the project for gamers, developers and publishers alike."

title: The Expanse: Osiris Reborn turns the best Mass Effect mission into an entire game
text:
I played an hour of The Expanse: Osiris Reborn at Gamescom, and despite doing it in a sweltering room with a dev judging me for every death, I came away pretty impressed. It deserves to stand on its own merits, but unfortunately I am about to talk about Mass Effect quite a lot—it's hard not to.
Like the BioWare of old, Owlcat is an isometric CRPG developer now trying its hand at a cinematic third-person RPG, which turns into a cover-heavy squad-based shooter when the guns come out. Mass Effect, then, is an obvious point of comparison.
(Image credit: Owlcat Games) But it's a comparison that serves The Expanse well, because in the short time I played it, I saw a multitude of ways in which it has improved upon BioWare's formula. How it handles exploration, combat and crew interactions makes me think, if it can keep it up, that The Expanse is going to make Mass Effect diehards extremely happy, without leaving Owlcat's CRPG fans out in the cold.
We already wrote about The Expanse's hi-tech fights after checking it out in April. "I was worried Owlcat couldn't pull off Mass Effect-style cinematic action in its big new RPG, but after an hour of blowing stuff up in The Expanse: Osiris Reborn, I'm feeling very reassured," Robin said back then. And I'm feeling the same way.
Mass Effect took three games to get its shooting up to snuff, but The Expanse might have nailed it on the first go. It's more responsive, varied, and you can order your teammates to pull off some explosively neat tricks. They're called exploits, and depending on who you have in your three-person squad, you'll see different parts of the environment highlighted in red—these are places where your pals can do their thing.
Double trouble
(Image credit: Owlcat Games) J, my identical twin who serves as the first companion, seems to mostly enjoy blowing things up. Usually that means cover. I was fighting Protogen goons—the villainous Earth corporation—and took every opportunity to stop them from cowardly hiding behind walls. But I also used J to take out bridges, a lift and other objects, with each instance rewarding me with a spectacular explosion and some dead foes.
A quick stun, a bullet in the head, job done.
Another companion sows chaos with their technical knowledge. If there are wires running underneath the floor in a combat area, they can electrify the floor and swiftly take out a bunch of enemies.
Not that I needed any help electrocuting people. I was playing as the engineer class, which allowed me to deploy turrets and drones. Midway through the demo, I got access to a new type of drone that could stun foes, which was a real game-changer when I started encountering dudes with flamethrowers that seemed to ignore cover. A quick stun, a bullet in the head, job done.
(Image credit: Owlcat Games) Unlike the previous demo, though, my Gamescom playthrough gave me lots of time for chatting and exploration. My twin and I were infiltrating a Protogen facility, disguised as employees of the titular Osiris organisation, so we didn't need to go in guns blazing.
The Expanse will see you putting together a crew for a heist, much in the same way Shep put one together for the suicide mission in Mass Effect 2. But even before you get to the actual heist, there are lots of smaller crimes and thematically adjacent missions that have the same heist energy.
I'm reminded of my favourite Mass Effect 2 loyalty mission, where you recruit Kasumi by helping her with a robbery. There are disguises, there's subterfuge, there's a lot of sticking it to rich dorks—it's a whole heap of fun. But that seems to just be a normal day in The Expanse, which is a thrilling prospect.
Team building
(Image credit: Owlcat Games) Anyway! Back to the infiltration. I was able to talk my way through most encounters with Protogen losers, and while The Expanse doesn't have the density of text or varied dialogue options of, say, Owlcat's Rogue Trader, I still felt able to make meaningful decisions and find different routes past obstacles.
When I needed to get into a crate, for instance, I failed to persuade a Protogen employee that it didn't matter that I had no paperwork. My persuasion skill wasn't high enough. But I was able to download some documents from a terminal, which one of my pals onboard my ship used to create a forgery.
This is possibly my favourite feature—that you have access to all these specialists who can lend you their expertise when you're off gallivanting on another mission. Interjections and offers of assistance seem common, too, making it feel like you're part of a proper heist crew. And sometimes it's just flavourful banter, allowing you to get a clearer picture of who these characters are, without you needing to walk up to them and have a full conversation.
(Image credit: Owlcat Games) Sometimes they'll have requests too, asking you to check something out that they've spotted on your feed. It's a level of teamwork that I haven't really seen represented in an RPG before, and one that gives your NPC pals a convincing illusion of agency.
Now I wish some of this stuff could have been in Mass Effect. You've got this crewed up ship, and that's cool, but outside of the companions you take with you on missions, the crew is barely even ancillary. Yes, you can date Kelly Chambers, and occasionally you'll hear from Joker or pre-android EDI when you're on a mission, but their participation is minimal. It's the same with your companions who you leave behind—they might as well not exist unless you're standing right next to them.
The Expanse, meanwhile, makes your companions just as critical to the mission as you, even when they're not with you in person. They are the solutions to your problems, they come up with plans, and they can even give you hints about how to take down a difficult enemy. By the end of the demo, I'd only met a couple of them in person, but I was already a fan of the whole bunch.
Spacecation
(Image credit: Owlcat Games) I really dug the quieter moments, too. At one point, we had to sneak through Ganymede's original colony, an underground warren that was constructed before the domes. Suddenly we'd gone from a corporate sci-fi thriller into something more horror-themed, slinking through dark, dilapidated ruins. It felt haunted.
I really dug the quieter moments, too.
Similarly, I enjoyed just wandering around the Protogen facility, when they still thought I was an ally. There's plenty of environmental storytelling and NPCs getting on with their day or having chats. With only an hour to spare, however, I had to start rushing through it, but I encountered quite a few diversions, locked doors and points of interest that I would have otherwise been keen to dive into.
If you've watched the show or read the books, you'll be rewarded for your foreknowledge with plenty of little nods here and there—especially when you're snooping around and reading everyone's emails. But if this is all new to you, it'll just appear to be worldbuilding rather than gatekeeping.
(Image credit: Owlcat Games) The demo ended on a cliffhanger, with my squad ready to pull off an audacious plan to stop a protomolecule mutant from doing more damage. I was ready to get stuck in, and then the "Thanks for playing" message appeared. It was devastating. I had to rush to another appointment anyway, but if Owlcat said "Nah, it's cool, you can play more," I don't think I would have been able to decline.
I guess I'll just have to wait until next year! The Expanse: Osiris Reborn should be appearing in the second quarter of 2027.

title: Total War: Warhammer 40,000's Space Marines will have to keep the Imperium happy and avoid looking too heretical
text:
One of the significant differences between most historical Total Wars and the Warhammer games is that the factions aren't comparable with nations. In Total War: Warhammer 40,000, the Space Marines and Astra Militarum, for instance, are effectively two branches of the same military.
So when I was playing Total War 40k at Gamescom as the Ultramarines, I noticed that my settlement garrison was full of just ordinary soldiers—members of the Planetary Defense Force. These units only served to defend the settlement, like a normal Total War garrison, but they weren't the same units that I could recruit as a Space Marine faction.
"The way that the Imperium works together is going to be very important," Dave Petry, battle product owner, told me. "And working as a Space Marine with local planetary forces and governors to be able to get the support that you need in order to be able to be that tip of the spear, we want that to be the case."
How the Imperium works, and your relationship to it, is still a work in progress, but Petry added that Creative Assembly has been playing around with concepts like "gaining support to be able to bring along units with you to fight your battles". So we might be able to bring in some meat shields from the PDF, or units from the Astra Militarum, to fight alongside our Space Marines.
I already saw a hint of this in the demo I played. In both the medium and massive-sized battles, my Space Marines arrived to find the Astra Militarum already fighting orks. I wasn't able to control them—they were just an allied force—but hopefully this is just a taste of something meatier.
Petry also teased what sounds like a reputation system. "Collaborating among the Imperium is something we really want to be able to do, and managing your reputation in the Imperium as a Space Marine is also something that's very important. Like not doing things that look too much like building an empire or becoming too powerful." So you'll need to keep the Imperium happy and avoid being accused of heresy.
Creative Assembly wants to "fill the galaxy out," says Petry, so we can expect to see other elements of the Imperium appearing. I'm really keeping my fingers crossed for some Adeptus Mechanicus fun in the near future. And the studio has already been teasing other Space Marine chapters, like my beloved Space Wolves, as well as xenos threats like Genestealer cults.
The good news is that you won't need to buy three games to see it all this time. Unlike Total War: Warhammer, Total War 40k is going to be a sandbox that Creative Assembly keeps adding to , rather than a series of separate games.

title: 好友照片共享应用「Retro」获2110万美元融资！这款聚焦反主流社交玩法的App，给社交赛道开发者带来哪些增长新思路？
text:
据媒体报道，好友照片共享应用「Retro」所属母公司 Lone Palm Labs 在 8 月公开的一份 SEC 文件显示，该公司已售出约 2110 万美元股权。同时据文件显示，该笔融资实际于去年12月完成，直至近期才通过备案文件对外公开。据数据机构PitchBook估算，目前该公司估值已突破1亿美元。
相比融资金额，这款App更值得我们关注的是它的产品演进路径。 据悉，「Retro」于2023年上线，主打私人照片日记功能，此后该App逐步拓展出私人群组相册、群组消息、内容回顾等功能。 且该产品不依靠广告变现，而是采用应用内订阅模式，其付费功能包括视频、GIF及贴纸评论支持、更多风格选项、无限历史记录访问以及专属应用图标等。
对于社交产品开发者来说，「Retro」也给大家带来了一些重要启发，接下来让我们一起来看一下~
「Retro」登上全球30多个市场iOS摄影与录像免费榜Top20
「Retro」最初并没有以无限信息流作为起点，而是以私人照片日记作为主要功能。 用户可以导入手机相册，回填过去数周的生活片段；好友列表、点赞功能默认保持私密，也不强制用户撰写文字文案。即便好友还没有全部加入，用户也可以获得个人记录、内容回顾的使用价值。
现如今产品又进一步打通了私人相册链接、群组消息、月度年度内容回顾、桌面小组件整套使用链路。在聚会、旅行等场景下，用户可以在原有群聊直接分享相册链接，再把“一次性事件”，沉淀为可以持续更新的小群空间。可以看到， 对用户来说，「Retro」扩张的并非公开粉丝数，而是愿意一起上传、共同产出照片内容的小群。
七麦数据监测显示，9 月 2 日 12 时，「Retro」占据全球 30 多个市场的 App Store 摄影与录像免费榜 Top20。在法国市场 App Store 摄影与录像免费榜，其近一个月排名实现大幅上涨，从第 209 升至第 2。
「Retro」在法国iOS摄影与录像免费榜近一个月排名趋势
「Retro」探索了一条密友社交应用的商业化新路径
「Retro」当前不依赖广告变现，而是面向高意向用户售卖增值功能。以其在美国区 App Store 产品页面信息为例，该 App 产品页面显示：月订阅定价 4.99 美元，年订阅 35.99 美元；付费权益包含视频使用权限、更多评论样式、更长周期的历史记录回溯等。
据第三方数据显示，「Retro」自上线以来累计下载量约达700万次，在过去180天内，应用内消费增幅已超过460%。同时据媒体分析报道，该 App 的付费订阅用户目前只占据整体用户的一小部分，但这部分用户被视为高黏性付费群体，已将「Retro」转变为日常高频使用的照片共享工具。
通过这款产品可以观察到， 密友社交赛道，并非只能走广告变现路线。先帮助用户积累值得回看的共同记忆，再围绕视频、历史记录、多样化表达等方面设计付费节点，商业化和关系密度可以顺着同一条产品路径同步推进。
这款产品给社交开发者带来了哪些增长启示？
那么「Retro」的增长、变现模式模式，给社交开发者带来了哪些具体的落地启发呢？
对开发者来说，首要目标不只是追逐注册用户总量，还需要打造 “建立真实社交关系后的有效激活”。 比如第一条好友邀请是否被接受、群组内是否出现双向的内容分享、第二周用户是否继续产生分享行为。
其次， 产品需要兼顾群内不同用户的行为。 密友群组中，既有主动输出内容的分享者，也有只浏览照片的围观家庭成员。参与门槛过低，会造成内容质量下滑；门槛设置过高，又会把低频参与用户挡在门外。比较稳妥的方式，是分开统计内容贡献者与浏览者的留存数据，再去测试轻量互动、消息提醒、权限配置等功能。
另外， 开发者可尝试把增长入口嵌入用户真实社交发生的场景 。比如家庭团聚、外出旅行、婚礼、亲子记录、兴趣小组等，都可以借助共享相册链接完成好友邀请。增长团队还可以利用 iTC 后台的产品页面优化工具测试不同场景素材，使用自定产品页面承接不同人群，再通过 App Analytics，观察商店产品页面转化以及发起邀请之后的用户激活效果。
结语
当下「Retro」释放出来的并不是“密友社交会取代公开社交”的信号，而是一套更为克制的产品运营和增长逻辑。
对于国内出海团队来说，社交赛道的增长机会不一定是打造又一个综合性社交大平台。家庭、旅行、亲子、婚礼、兴趣小组这类关系明确、天然会产生内容的垂直场景，更适合优先验证关系密度，再逐步扩大分发规模。
你的社交产品，从中得到了哪些启发呢？
